title: Grade 4 Science — Fri, May 29
description: Rocks & Minerals — Day 5 of 5: Synthesis — uses, identification, and the cycle
subject: science

questions.question: Classify these rocks: Granite / Marble / Sandstone
questions.explanation: Granite = igneous (cooled magma). Marble = metamorphic (limestone transformed). Sandstone = sedimentary (sand cemented).

questions.question: Rock has layers, contains a fossil shell. What type is it, and how did it form?
options: Sedimentary — layers of sediment compressed over time
questions.explanation: Layers + fossil = sedimentary. Fossils only survive in sedimentary rock because igneous and metamorphic processes destroy them.

questions.question: You find a very hard, crystalline rock with no layers and no fossils near an old volcano. What is it most likely?
questions.explanation: Near a volcano, crystalline, no layers, no fossils → igneous. Basalt is a common volcanic igneous rock.

questions.question: Which sequence is correct in the rock cycle?
options: Igneous → Heat+Pressure → Metamorphic → Melt → Magma → Igneous again
questions.explanation: One valid cycle: Igneous rock buried deep → heat+pressure → Metamorphic → intense heat → Melts → Magma → erupts → Igneous again.

questions.question: Match mineral to use: Diamond / Graphite / Quartz / Mica
options: Diamond=cutting tools+jewels; Graphite=pencils; Quartz=glass+electronics; Mica=electrical insulation
questions.explanation: Diamond (hardest → cutting, jewels). Graphite (soft, marks → pencils). Quartz (SiO₂ → glass, chips). Mica (splits thin → insulation, cosmetics).

questions.question: Why can't fossils form in igneous rock?
options: The extreme heat of lava/magma destroys any organisms
questions.explanation: Molten lava/magma temperatures (700–1300°C) instantly destroy any living organisms, so no fossils can be preserved.

questions.question: A rock sample has swirly, banded patterns and no layers. It is very hard. What is it?
questions.explanation: Swirly/banded patterns without clear sedimentary layers + hard = metamorphic. Gneiss and schist are classic examples.

questions.question: Tadgola village has a sandstone quarry. What product would NOT be made from this rock?
questions.explanation: Sandstone is not a gemstone — it is used for building and carving, not jewellery. Diamonds, rubies, and sapphires are gemstones.

questions.question: The Taj Mahal is made of white marble. What original rock was marble before it was transformed?
questions.explanation: Marble forms from limestone (sedimentary) under heat and pressure. The Taj Mahal's white marble was once limestone.

questions.question: Riya finds a rock that: scratches glass, has metallic luster, is heavy. Which mineral is she likely holding?
questions.explanation: Scratches glass (hard), metallic luster, heavy → iron ore / hematite. Talc and graphite are soft; calcite does not have metallic luster.

questions.question: How do humans use the rock cycle?
options: We control the rock cycle with machines
We cannot use the rock cycle
We extract minerals from rocks formed by the cycle (mining) and use the materials
We speed up the rock cycle
questions.explanation: Humans mine coal, iron, limestone, diamonds, etc. — all formed by rock cycle processes. We depend on these materials without controlling the cycle.

questions.question: Granite is used for kitchen countertops because it is hard. Marble is used for sculptures. Both are used in construction. What type are they?
questions.explanation: Granite = igneous (cooled magma, very hard). Marble = metamorphic (limestone transformed). Both are valued for durability and appearance.

questions.question: If all volcanic activity stopped forever, which rock type would eventually stop forming?
questions.explanation: Igneous rock needs magma/lava. No volcanoes = no new igneous rock. Sedimentary and metamorphic could still form from existing rocks.

questions.question: Week scenario: Ocean floor basalt gets subducted (goes under continent), melts, rises as magma, erupts. Full rock cycle path?
options: Igneous (basalt) → Subduction → Melt → Magma → New Igneous rock
Cannot happen in the rock cycle
questions.explanation: Basalt (igneous) on ocean floor is subducted into the mantle → melts into magma → rises → erupts → new igneous rock. Direct igneous→magma→igneous path.

questions.question: Best summary of this week's learning about rocks and minerals:
options: Rocks and minerals are the same; there is only one type of rock
Three rock types form by different processes; minerals are their building blocks; the rock cycle continuously recycles Earth's material
questions.explanation: Week synthesis: 3 rock types (igneous/sedimentary/metamorphic), each with distinct formation processes. Minerals = rock ingredients. Rock cycle = continuous transformation over geological time.
